short: adds whole rows to a table: name the columns, give the values, one row or many per statement.
the value a column gets when an INSERT leaves it out or asks for it by name. NULL if the column declares none.
fills a table from a query's result in one statement, without the rows ever leaving the database.
a counter object that hands out numbers with nextval. it never takes one back, so rollbacks leave gaps.
changes columns in every row its WHERE matches. no WHERE matches every row, and the tag says how many.
removes every row its WHERE matches. the rows stay on their pages, marked deleted, until VACUUM.
empties a table by swapping in a new empty file: instant, no dead rows, but an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock and no WHERE.
makes INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or MERGE hand back the rows it changed, in the same round trip.
in RETURNING since postgres 18, the row before and after the change. in a trigger, the same two rows.
an INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or MERGE inside WITH, whose RETURNING rows feed the rest of the statement.
insert a row, or update the one already there with that key. in postgres: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE.
the INSERT clause that says what to do when a unique index finds the key taken: DO NOTHING or DO UPDATE.
inside ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, the row you tried to insert, as opposed to the row already in the table.
the unique index ON CONFLICT uses to detect a conflict, and to wait on another session's uncommitted insert.
syncs a target table with a source: WHEN MATCHED, WHEN NOT MATCHED and WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE clauses, one statement.
moves rows in bulk between a table and a file or a client stream, in one statement, without parsing each row as SQL.
a table that writes no WAL: faster to load, not replicated, and emptied after a crash.
user input that ends up parsed as SQL, because it was glued into the query text instead of bound as a value.
a $1-style slot in a statement whose value is sent separately, after parsing, so it can only ever be a value.
a statement parsed once with parameter slots and run many times with different values. PREPARE and EXECUTE in SQL.
the wire protocol drivers use for parameters: Parse the SQL, Bind the values, Execute. one statement per Parse.
a function's promise: IMMUTABLE (same input, same output, forever), STABLE (within a statement) or VOLATILE.
the planner pasting a simple LANGUAGE sql function's body into the query, so it plans as if you'd typed it out.
a function body written as SQL statements (RETURN, BEGIN ATOMIC), parsed once and tracked as a dependency.
postgres's built-in procedural language: variables, IF, loops and exception handling, run inside the server.
a named routine run with CALL. unlike a function it can COMMIT partway through, if not called inside BEGIN.
a transaction inside a transaction, as a savepoint or a PL/pgSQL EXCEPTION block starts. it gets its own xid if it writes.
a function the database runs automatically on INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE, before or after, per row or per statement.
the old or new rows of a whole statement, handed to an AFTER statement trigger through REFERENCING.
